children.title: Jan-99
children.summary: Jan-00 Jan-01 Jan-02 Jan-03 Jan-04 Jan-05 ($80) The principal driver behind the rising spread between crude and bunker prices since 2003 is the rapidly escalating price of crude oil. The growing demand for resids in China to fuel its economy has increased bunker prices, but not to the extent of the increased price of crude, which may be reflecting the world of oil hitting supply capacity constraints.

children.title: Bunkers Going Bonkers?
children.summary: Yes, in absolute terms the cost of bunkers has escalated; no, in relative terms compared to spot WS rates at today's robust levels. Owners are still making plenty of money and giving up a few extra WS points to the bunker suppliers can't be hurting that much.
